question: What subjects are said to be treated in the thirty-first and thirty-second chapters?
premises: The thirty-first chapter is said to state certain matters in detail.
The thirty-second chapter treats distinctions of quality and principality.
The thirty-second chapter also treats own-nature and the worship of power.
inference: The overview assigns detailed exposition to the thirty-first chapter and doctrinal distinctions, nature, and power-worship to the thirty-second.
uncertainties: The precise referent of guṇapradhānatābhedāḥ depends on the later chapter's context.
plain_english: These matters are to be explained in detail in the thirty-first chapter. In the thirty-second chapter are set forth the distinctions of quality and principality, their own nature, and the worship of their power.
